result.title: Beyond Flat Walks: Compositional Abstraction for Autoregressive Graph Generation
result.summary: Autoregressive graph generators typically linearize graphs through flat node-edge walks, which can obscure higher-order structure in large and complex graphs. We introduce a hierarchical graph abstraction and coarse-to-fine generation pipeline that separates coarsening, tokenization, and decoding. This exposes three design axes: community coarsening, hierarchical tokenization, and order randomization. Across these axes, traversal-based hierarchy consistently improves distributional and structural fidelity, while its V.U.N.\ cost depends strongly on the coarsening and randomization policy. In particular, the fidelity--V.U.N.\ trade-off observed under within-community randomization is substantially reduced when traversal order is randomized across the full hierarchy. With a fixed backbone, training protocol, and matched training time across five molecular and five non-molecular benchmarks, hierarchical serialization yields consistent distributional and structural gains on all molecular datasets, while the non-molecular results further show that these gains depend on how well the supplied hierarchy aligns with structure in the target distribution. Together, these results characterize when and how hierarchical serialization benefits autoregressive graph generation.

AI.brief_summary: 论文提出层次化图抽象与由粗到细的自回归图生成流程，把社区粗化、层次化 tokenization 与解码拆成三个设计轴，并在五个分子与五个非分子基准上分析结构保真度与 V.U.N. 成本的权衡。
AI.relevance_reason: 其「由粗到细」的层次化序列化与状态抽象可能为 LVR 中 latent 推理状态的分层组织、更新顺序及计算成本分配提供概念线索；但研究对象是图生成而非多模态推理，迁移可行性需要核查。
